```{r}
#| include: false

options(warn = 2)

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)

task_map <- read_csv(
  "data/periodic_table.csv",
  col_types = cols(
    task_number = col_integer(),
    symbol = col_character(),
    title = col_character(),
    item_type = col_character(),
    group_id = col_integer(),
    group_name = col_character(),
    stage = col_character(),
    lesson_path = col_character(),
    status = col_character(),
    last_reviewed = col_character()
  ),
  na = character()
)

available <- task_map |>
  filter(status == "available")

planned <- task_map |>
  filter(status == "planned")

availability_sentence <- if (nrow(planned) == 0L) {
  sprintf("All %d lessons are written.", nrow(task_map))
} else {
  sprintf(
    paste(
      "%d of the %d lessons are written. The rest are planned.",
      "Their tiles remain visible until the lessons are available."
    ),
    nrow(available),
    nrow(task_map)
  )
}
```

**Natural language processing (NLP)** is the study of how computers process
human language. These lessons explain text tasks through R examples.
Select a tile to read a lesson.

## The tasks {#periodic-table-heading}

Related tasks share a column. The six stages cover source data, language
structure, models, generation, systems, and visualization.
Position groups related subjects. It does not rank methods or prescribe a
workflow. `r availability_sentence`

::: {.callout-tip}
## Start here

For a course, read in number order. Later examples use R concepts from earlier
lessons. For a specific problem, open the relevant lesson. Each page explains
its NLP concept and assumptions.

For model-assisted analysis, read
[Using a language model in a reproducible analysis](using-language-models.qmd).
The guide explains model records and compares model labels with a sample
examined by a person.

For whole-system evaluation, read
[Beyond the periodic table](advanced/index.qmd).
Its first lesson compares two versions in R and applies a release rule.
:::

**Beyond individual tasks:**
[Beyond the periodic table](advanced/index.qmd) explains systems, tools, and
evaluation.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

group_sizes <- task_map |>
  count(group_id) |>
  pull(n)

expected_group_sizes <- c(
  7L, 6L, 5L, 5L, 5L,
  6L, 4L, 4L, 5L, 5L,
  5L, 5L, 6L, 6L, 7L
)

lesson_sources <- available |>
  pull(lesson_path) |>
  str_replace("[.]html$", ".qmd")

stopifnot(
  identical(getOption("warn"), 2L),
  inherits(task_map, "tbl_df"),
  identical(task_map$task_number, 1:81),
  identical(sort(unique(task_map$group_id)), 1:15),
  identical(group_sizes, expected_group_sizes),
  identical(
    which(task_map$status == "available"),
    seq_len(nrow(available))
  ),
  identical(length(unique(task_map$symbol)), 81L),
  all(task_map$status %in% c("available", "planned")),
  all(nzchar(available$lesson_path)),
  all(planned$lesson_path == ""),
  all(nzchar(available$last_reviewed)),
  all(file.exists(lesson_sources))
)

escape_text <- function(value) {
  as.character(htmltools::htmlEscape(value))
}

escape_attribute <- function(value) {
  as.character(
    htmltools::htmlEscape(value, attribute = TRUE)
  )
}

stage_labels <- c(
  source = "Source and training data",
  language = "Language structure",
  model = "Models and analysis",
  generation = "Language generation",
  systems = "Language systems",
  visualization = "Visualization"
)

stopifnot(
  all(unique(task_map$stage) %in% names(stage_labels))
)

render_tile <- function(task_number,
                        symbol,
                        title,
                        item_type,
                        lesson_path,
                        status,
                        ...) {
  is_available <- identical(status, "available")
  label_text <- if (is_available) "Read lesson" else "Planned"
  status_class <- "element-status"

  tile_contents <- sprintf(
    paste0(
      '<span class="element-number">%d</span>',
      '<span class="element-kind">%s</span>',
      '<span class="element-symbol" aria-hidden="true">%s</span>',
      '<span class="element-name">%s</span>',
      '<span class="%s">%s</span>'
    ),
    task_number,
    escape_text(item_type),
    escape_text(symbol),
    escape_text(title),
    status_class,
    label_text
  )

  tile <- if (is_available) {
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<a class="nlp-element is-available" ',
        'data-task-number="%d" data-item-type="%s" ',
        'data-status="available" ',
        'href="%s" aria-label="%s">%s</a>'
      ),
      task_number,
      escape_attribute(item_type),
      escape_attribute(lesson_path),
      escape_attribute(
        sprintf(
          "Task %d. %s. Item type: %s. %s.",
          task_number,
          title,
          item_type,
          label_text
        )
      ),
      tile_contents
    )
  } else {
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<div class="nlp-element is-planned" ',
        'data-task-number="%d" data-item-type="%s" ',
        'data-status="planned">%s</div>'
      ),
      task_number,
      escape_attribute(item_type),
      tile_contents
    )
  }

  paste0('<li class="element-slot">', tile, "</li>")
}

render_group <- function(group_rows) {
  group_id <- unique(group_rows$group_id)
  group_name <- unique(group_rows$group_name)
  stage <- unique(group_rows$stage)
  stage_label <- unname(stage_labels[stage])
  heading_id <- sprintf("task-group-%d", group_id)

  stopifnot(
    identical(length(group_id), 1L),
    identical(length(group_name), 1L),
    identical(length(stage), 1L),
    identical(length(stage_label), 1L)
  )

  tiles <- group_rows |>
    pmap_chr(render_tile) |>
    paste(collapse = "")

  paste0(
    sprintf(
      '<section class="element-group stage-%s" aria-labelledby="%s">',
      escape_attribute(stage),
      heading_id
    ),
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<h3 class="element-group-title" id="%s">',
        '<span class="element-stage">%s</span>',
        '<span class="element-group-name">%s</span>',
        '</h3>'
      ),
      heading_id,
      escape_text(stage_label),
      escape_text(group_name)
    ),
    '<ol class="element-stack">',
    tiles,
    "</ol></section>"
  )
}

stage_key <- stage_labels |>
  imap_chr(function(label, stage) {
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<span class="task-map-stage-key-item stage-%s">',
        '<span class="task-map-stage-swatch" aria-hidden="true"></span>',
        '%s</span>'
      ),
      escape_attribute(stage),
      escape_text(label)
    )
  }) |>
  paste(collapse = "")

groups <- task_map |>
  arrange(group_id, task_number) |>
  group_by(group_id) |>
  group_split()

table_html <- groups |>
  map_chr(render_group) |>
  paste(collapse = "")

stage_routes <- available |>
  group_by(stage) |>
  slice_min(task_number, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(task_number) |>
  mutate(
    link = sprintf(
      '<a href="%s">%s</a>',
      escape_attribute(lesson_path),
      escape_text(str_to_lower(unname(stage_labels[stage])))
    )
  ) |>
  pull(link)

route_html <- paste(stage_routes, collapse = ", ")

stopifnot(
  identical(length(groups), 15L),
  identical(
    length(stage_routes),
    length(unique(available$stage))
  ),
  identical(
    str_count(table_html, fixed('class="element-slot"')),
    81L
  ),
  identical(
    str_count(table_html, fixed('class="nlp-element is-available"')),
    nrow(available)
  )
)

planned_key <- if (nrow(planned) > 0L) {
  paste0(
    '<span class="task-map-key-item">',
    '<span class="task-map-key-swatch" aria-hidden="true"></span>',
    "Lesson planned",
    "</span>"
  )
} else {
  ""
}

planned_instruction <- if (nrow(planned) > 0L) {
  "Dashed tiles are planned. "
} else {
  ""
}

cat(
  '<div class="task-map-key">',
  '<span class="task-map-key-item">',
  '<span class="task-map-key-swatch available" aria-hidden="true"></span>',
  'Read lesson',
  '</span>',
  planned_key,
  '</div>',
  '<div class="task-map-stage-key" aria-label="Task stages">',
  stage_key,
  '</div>',
  '<p class="task-map-instructions" id="task-map-instructions">',
  'Select a solid-bordered tile to open its lesson. ',
  planned_instruction,
  'If the whole map does not fit, ',
  'use the buttons, arrow keys, or horizontal scrolling.',
  '</p>',
  '<div class="task-map-scroll-controls" ',
  'aria-label="Move through task groups">',
  '<button type="button" data-map-direction="-1" ',
  'aria-controls="nlp-task-map">Earlier groups</button>',
  '<button type="button" data-map-direction="1" ',
  'aria-controls="nlp-task-map">Later groups</button>',
  '</div>',
  '<div class="periodic-scroll" id="nlp-task-map" ',
  'tabindex="0" role="region" ',
  'aria-label="Periodic table of NLP tasks" ',
  'aria-describedby="task-map-instructions">',
  '<div class="periodic-table">',
  table_html,
  '</div></div>',
  '<nav class="available-routes" aria-label="Ways into the map">',
  '<p class="route-item">',
  '<strong>Read as a course.</strong> ',
  '<a href="1_source_data_loading/01-bits-to-character-encoding.html">',
  'Start at task 1</a>. Then read the lessons in number order. ',
  'Each lesson uses R concepts from earlier lessons.',
  '</p>',
  '<p class="route-item">',
  '<strong>Solve one problem.</strong> ',
  'Select the stage for your task: ',
  route_html,
  '. Each lesson explains its NLP concept and assumptions.',
  '</p>',
  '<p class="route-item">',
  '<strong>Find one task.</strong> ',
  'Find the task in the map. Read its lesson. ',
  'Each lesson states its limits and what its results do not show.',
  '</p>',
  '</nav>',
  sep = ""
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What this map is

This is a teaching aid, not a scientific taxonomy or a complete account of the
field. A **taxonomy** is a system of classification.
The map includes tasks, methods, objectives, resources, services,
applications, and work throughout a model's life. Each tile names its item
type. Some inherited group names describe different types of work.
The relevant lessons explain these limits.
:::

## Why these lessons exist

Suppose your director asks how many of last quarter's 40,000 customer comments
are complaints. Next quarter's support budget depends on the answer.
An AI assistant reports 22 percent. You still need evidence that the estimate
is useful for this decision.

First, give the meaning of a complaint. Decide whether the category includes a blunt
question, a partly critical compliment, or a report of a broken link.
Every model run applies a definition to all 40,000 comments, even if nobody
chose that definition explicitly. A more capable model cannot decide what you
intended to measure.

Next, examine the uncertainty in "about 22 percent." You can compare automatic
answers with a sample of the same material that a person examined.
The conclusions depend on the sampling method and the rules for people who give labels.
Some methods calculate error estimates from agreement among automatic labellers.
Those estimates depend on assumptions about how the errors relate.
A person might need to examine examples to evaluate those assumptions.

Also examine the input text. Each result describes the version of the text that
the software received. Transfers between systems can damage characters.
A comma can split a row. Text extraction can read a scanned digit as a letter.

These failures do not always produce an error message. The answer can change
and still look reasonable. Lessons 1, 3 and 7 deliberately produce these
failures so that you can examine them.

You must still decide what to measure, which material to use, and when to
reject a result. These decisions give a tool its instructions.
You also use these decisions to accept or reject its output.

You can buy data with labels or hire an annotation service. A model can also
give labels to many kinds of text, although it can refuse some requests.
These services can report agreement scores for their labels.
An agreement score does not explain every limit of those labels.
Calculating scores on your own text helps you understand their limits.

You do not have to do all the work by hand. Tools can help with drafts,
summaries, and unfamiliar text. The checks must match the decision.
Examine the definition, the comparison, and the received text.
The necessary checks depend on your text and the cost of a wrong answer.
This page cannot choose them for you.

The guide [Using a language model in a reproducible analysis](using-language-models.qmd)
applies these checks to a constructed collection. It records a local model
as a measurement instrument. It compares model labels with a random sample
examined by a person. It then corrects an estimate for the errors found in
that sample.

Lessons 1 through 13 cover text collection from files, web pages, and scans,
then the creation of labels. Lessons 14 through 42 cover words, grammar,
phrases, entities, sentences, paragraphs, and documents. These lessons explain
what each transformation helps you do and what information it can remove.

Lessons 43 through 68 cover models for classification, discovery, comparison,
and text generation. Each result has a baseline or a stated limit.
Lessons 69 through 74 combine tasks into small systems. Examples include
relation extraction, a knowledge base, question answering, dialogue, search,
and document review with a recall estimate.
Lessons 75 through 81 present results through an app, annotated text, charts,
maps, and graphs. They explain the conclusions each display permits.

## About this site

**Available** means a lesson source exists and its project-recorded automated
checks passed. Those `passed` values are project assertions, not independent
certification. Manual accessibility tests and final human approval remain pending.
The separate status fields are in `data/lesson_reviews.csv`.

Methods in this field change quickly. A lesson states which claims can change
over time and gives a date. The publishing rules are in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/farach/periodic_table_nlp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
and
[RESEARCH_STANDARDS.md](https://github.com/farach/periodic_table_nlp/blob/main/RESEARCH_STANDARDS.md).

This repository builds the source and does automated checks, but does not deploy it. The
canonical published location is
[workforcefutures.net/learn/nlp/](https://workforcefutures.net/learn/nlp/).
A successful build produces a rendered site. It does not prove that the
published site is current or that pending manual checks passed.

The task names and groupings are adapted from Rob van Zoest's
[Periodic Table of NLP Tasks](https://www.innerdoc.com/periodic-table-of-nlp-tasks/).
That page states no licence and invites reuse. The task names are standard
terms in the field. This project's grouping, wording, interface, and lessons
are separate work. This project is responsible for errors in that work.
If the original author prefers different terms, this site will use them.
